components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true

          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type

        - timestamp

## Summary

I implemented telephone normalization so numbers are stored digits-only, returned as stored, and normalized before the uniqueness check.

**Changes:**

1. **`src/main/resources/openapi.yml`** — Relaxed the `telephone` validation pattern from `^[0-9]*$` to `^[0-9 ()-]*$`. Without this, a formatted number like `(613) 555-0100` would fail `@Valid` binding and return 400 before any normalization could run. (The regenerated `OwnerFieldsDto` picks this up on build.)

2. **`.../function/owner/TelephoneNormalizer.java`** (new) — Small utility with `digitsOnly(String)` that strips all non-digit characters (spaces, dashes, parentheses, etc.), null-safe.

3. **`BuildOwner.java`** (POST/create) — Normalizes the mapped owner's telephone to digits-only immediately after mapping, *before* `RejectDuplicateOwner` runs. So the stored value is digits-only and the uniqueness comparison sees the normalized form — `(613) 555-0100` and `6135550100` collide and the second is rejected 409.

4. **`ApplyOwner.java`** (PUT/update) — Same normalization applied on update, keeping stored telephones consistently digits-only.

The existing `RejectDuplicateOwner` / `DuplicateMatching` comparison then operates on already-normalized values, so the uniqueness check works correctly. Both new Cp11 tests (`coreStoresDigitsOnly`, `functionalityNormalisedDuplicateRejected`) pass, and no existing tests regressed.
